name: Liraglutide
route_note: subcutaneous injection once daily (up to 1.8 mg for diabetes; 3.0 mg for weight management)
owner: Novo Nordisk; generics in the US

discovery.by: Novo Nordisk (team including Lotte Bjerre Knudsen)
discovery.note: Human GLP-1 analogue with Arg34 substitution and a C16 palmitic acid attached at Lys26, enabling albumin binding.

tagline: Once-daily GLP-1 analogue, the first shown to cut cardiovascular events (LEADER)
summary: Liraglutide is a once-daily GLP-1 receptor agonist with 97% homology to human GLP-1, used for type 2 diabetes (Victoza) and chronic weight management (Saxenda). In the LEADER trial it reduced major cardiovascular events and death, and it was the first GLP-1 agonist approved for obesity.
mechanism: Liraglutide activates the GLP-1 receptor, increasing glucose-dependent insulin secretion, lowering glucagon and slowing gastric emptying. A fatty-acid chain lets it bind albumin and self-associate into heptamers at the injection site, protecting it from DPP-4 and renal clearance and giving a half-life of about 13 hours.
Through brain GLP-1 receptors in the hypothalamus and hindbrain the drug also reduces appetite and food intake, and it slows gastric emptying; together these effects produce weight loss.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (adults and children 10 years and older)
Reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular disease
Chronic weight management in obesity or overweight with comorbidity (Saxenda; adults and adolescents 12+)

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: The European Commission approves Victoza in June 2009.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Victoza in January 2010 with a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumours.

history.title: Saxenda for obesity
history.detail: FDA approves liraglutide 3.0 mg (Saxenda) for chronic weight management in December 2014.

history.title: LEADER
history.detail: LEADER shows a 13% reduction in major cardiovascular events versus placebo (NEJM 2016).

history.title: Cardiovascular indication
history.detail: FDA adds a cardiovascular risk-reduction indication to Victoza.

history.title: Paediatric use
history.detail: Victoza becomes the first non-insulin drug approved for type 2 diabetes in children since metformin.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: An authorised generic of Victoza launches in mid-2024 and FDA approves the first generic liraglutide in December 2024.

pk.metabolism: proteolysis by DPP-4 and neutral endopeptidases
pk.excretion: metabolites in urine and faeces; no intact drug

safety.boxed_warning: Risk of thyroid C-cell tumours: caused C-cell tumours in rodents; contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

facts: Saxenda (2014) was the first GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for chronic weight management.
Liraglutide was the first GLP-1 agonist to show cardiovascular benefit in a dedicated outcomes trial (LEADER, 2016).
